articles.text:
2. About electrical Equipment

Electric current (voltage) in Japan is 100-110, which is about 9% lower than in the U.S., which is 110-120. In the western half of Japan (Kyoto, Osaka, Kobe, etc.), the cycles are the same as in the U.S.-- 60 cycles. However, 50 cycles is normal in the eastern half of the country, including Tokyo. Therefore, if you work in Tokyo and want to send or take electrical appliances with motors from the U.S., you will need to have them adjusted in Japan before using them. Electric clocks are often impractical to convert. Many appliances, such as toasters, are not affected by cycle level.
